title: Oil Filter Housing with an Integral Debris Sampling Port
abstract: A sampling port cast into the oil filter housing so that a debris sample can be drawn without opening the filter bowl, cutting the oil loss and the contamination risk of the current sampling task.

sections.reason: Oil debris sampling currently requires the filter bowl to be opened, which loses about 1.5 litres of oil, exposes the element to hangar air and takes a technician forty minutes per engine. Operators sample at every A-check under the engine health programme, so the task is frequent. Three operators have reported filter element contamination traced to the sampling task itself rather than to the engine, and two of those events led to an unnecessary element change. A port that lets the sample be drawn from the housing without opening it removes the whole failure mode.
sections.description: The filter housing is re-cast with a sampling port on the upstream side, closed by a self-sealing coupling that accepts the standard sampling adapter. The housing supply duct D7920125546052 is replaced by an item with the port boss, the housing seal D7920124401801 is re-profiled where the boss interrupts the sealing land, and clamp EN635637-80 secures the sample line stub to the existing bracket. The oil distribution duct 22EO and the pump seal 5409EO keep their identifiers. Revised detail is on drawings D79201225675 and D79201258886. Work is done with the fan cowl doors open, zones 411, 421 and 452, and no engine removal is needed.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.7 kg per engine, so 1.4 kg per aircraft, symmetric. No electrical load change. The housing is not interchangeable with the current item because the port boss changes the external envelope at the cowl clearance line, and the clearance to the cowl acoustic panel is the tightest point of the installation. Sampling task time falls from about forty minutes to twelve per engine and the oil loss per sample is eliminated. Maintenance manual content for oil sampling has to be re-issued and the illustrated parts figure needs the new housing.
sections.embodiment_note: Launched for production cut-in and spares only. A retrofit campaign is not proposed because the housing is normally changed at a shop visit, and operators are expected to take the new standard as their existing housings are replaced.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm the clearance between the port boss and the cowl acoustic panel with the cowl closed and hot, whether the self-sealing coupling is compatible with the sampling adapters already in operator tooling stocks, and whether the oil system trouble shooting content needs a new step to exclude a leaking coupling.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at the next engine build standard change
